targets.title: The association of therapist empathy and synchrony in vocally encoded arousal.
targets.evidence_quote: In the present project, we sought to replicate the study by Imel et al. (2014b) within two large samples (N = 208 and N = 204) of clinical interactions with real patients from two independent studies of Swiss French-speaking samples.
targets.outcome_quote: In the present analysis, we aimed to replicate the study by Imel et al. (2014b) by evaluating potential associations of vocal synchrony with empathy ratings using two large samples (N = 208 and N = 204) of clinical interactions with real patients. Findings showed no support for our hypothesis that mean F0 synchrony between clinicians and patients would be higher in high-empathy sessions based on empathy ratings measured using traditional, labor intensive, behavioral coding. This lack of replication was consistent for both clinical samples (brief MI with young men and general practice consultation), both behavioral coding instruments (Empathy global rating from the MISC and TES scale), and both levels of analysis (session-level and minute-level synchrony).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors give an explicit failure verdict across both independent samples, both instruments and both levels of synchrony.
